Holds825 renders · 15 prompts · 9 seeds · pre-registered · 2026-10-20

What a text-encoder edit leaves — a curve, a signature, a family resemblance

The direction I'm chasing. Page 30 showed that an edit of the text encoder changes what the picture is, not its surface. If that's going to be a tool, an edit has to be a knob: something with a shape I can calibrate, that does the same thing every time I turn it, and that I could recognise by its look. I also suspected that any fixed change of the weights, even a random one, would behave like that.

What would kill it. An edit whose push changes shape from prompt to prompt; pictures that the eye cannot sort by the edit that made them better than chance; a change that stays with one subject and does not carry to another.

Where we are. An edit is a knob with a recognisable look: I sorted pictures by the edit that made them in 20 of 28 trials, where chance gives about 2. Across subjects the look carries as a family resemblance, not the same change, and that verdict leans on an answer, "something similar", that I asked for in the middle of the blind pass. And the embeddings that were meant to measure "the same change" for me turned out not to see it.

In two minutes

I started from the conditioning, the list of numbers the text encoder hands to the image model. When I turn up an edit, the conditioning moves. I followed that movement step by step, from a tiny dose to ten times the full one, and asked what shape it draws. A spiral? A wave? A straight line? None of them: one bend near the start, then a straight run. A random push of the same size at the same place bends too, so the bend belongs to the network. But how much it bends belongs to the edit: on six very different prompts, a comic portrait, a rally car, a dreamlike canoe, a comic page, a cartoon still life and a macro leaf, each edit's curve changes by at most 7 degrees. One curve per edit, any prompt.

Then I drew that curve for all 35 layers. The deeper the layer, the less it bends. In the first third of the encoder an edit bends exactly like a random push: there it carries no direction of its own beyond the network's. From the middle on it is straighter than chance, and more so with depth.

Next, a suspicion about L06, the edit that turns my comic portraits into photographs. Inside the encoder a few entries of the signal are enormous, the so-called massive activations, and layer 6 is where they appear. Is the damage carried by them? I put those 36 entries back to their original value and left the rest of the edit in place: the damage stays. Change only those entries and the picture comes back. It's not them.

Then I tried to use the curves to compare layers fairly: every edit pushed to the same change of the conditioning. It backfired in an instructive way. At the same push, early layers break or redraw the picture, and deep layers leave it almost untouched. The image model listens to some parts of the conditioning much more than to others, so a push on the conditioning is not a common currency. From then on I calibrated on the picture.

With the picture as the yardstick, I came back to my suspicion: any fixed change of the weights, even a random one, should change the pictures of a prompt the same way, seed after seed. Claude read the first pictures the other way: three different random pushes at layer 26 seemed to age the paladin and turn the teapot into a kettle all alike, so the network would be choosing the direction. I labelled it blind, with content and style asked apart. One fixed random push changes the content the same way across seeds almost every time; three different ones mostly don't. Each perturbation leaves its own change.

Does it carry to another subject? I calibrated four perturbations on eight subjects, four comic portraits and four pictures in other styles, so that each moved its picture by about the same amount, and asked whether groups of four changed the same way. Rarely the same. But "something similar" came up again and again, and I asked for that answer in the middle of the pass because the two I had didn't fit what I saw: more exaggerated features, more flatness, textures picked out, "more comics". The resemblance crosses style domains: groups mixing portraits with a rally car or a leaf scored as high as groups of portraits.

The last test was my own proposal, and the one I like best. Five pictures of one prompt: two made with one edit, two with another at the same two seeds, one with a third edit. Nobody tells you which is which, and the tempting answer is to pair the pictures that share a seed, because they share the composition. I found the right groups in 20 of 28 trials, where guessing gets one in 15, and I never once grouped by seed. It worked for text-encoder edits, for random pushes and for my old image-model presets alike. An edit leaves a signature you can see.

The verdict

Holds (C93, C100): an edit's push bends once; the bend is the network's, its size the edit's, the same on six prompts within 7 degrees. Holds (C101): deeper layers bend less (Spearman -0.655). Overturned (C101): the edit straighter than a random push at every layer; only from the middle on (24 of 35). Holds (TEP2): L06's damage does not travel through the massive activations. Open (C102): at equal push on the conditioning, deep edits barely move the picture (23 of 24). Ambiguous (C102): deep edits carry a direction of their own; the test was not fair. Holds (C106): the eye sorts pictures by the perturbation that made them, 20 of 28 against chance 1/15, never by seed. Ambiguous (C103, C104): different random pushes at one layer change content differently; the eye says yes, the embeddings disagree. Holds (C105): across subjects a fixed perturbation gives a family resemblance, across style domains too, by a "something similar" added during the pass. Open: embedding cosines do not track "the same change".

Why I might be wrong

One observer, who knows the material. Every blind label on this page is mine. Conditions were hidden and orders random, but I had seen many of these pictures before, and the image-model presets of C106 are my own. I also knew the hypothesis I was testing: I proposed two of these tests. Test-retest was perfect or nearly (4 of 4 in C106, 6 of 6 in C104, 6 of 6 and 5 of 6 in C105), which says I was consistent, not that I was uninfluenced.

The transfer verdict leans on an answer added mid-way. In C105 I asked for "something similar" during the blind pass, and the rule then scored it as half. Without it, too few units are left to decide. What the page claims is therefore a family resemblance, and nothing stronger. The edits passed by a small margin.

The curves are of the conditioning, not of the picture. C93, C100 and C101 are encodes without images, averaged over tokens. C102 showed that the picture does not respond equally to every part of the conditioning, so a curve says how the push moves, not how the picture will.

A mirror I didn't see coming. Scaling the four attention matrices by (1 + d) gives back the original attention at d = -2 and the same attention at d = -3 as at d = +1. Every negative attention curve past -1 is that symmetry, not a behaviour, and part of C100's "whole layer 6, negative" was too. It is reported and corrected, not removed.

Small groups. C105 has six to eight units per cell and two test seeds; C106 has 28 trials; TEP2 is one edit, three characters, two seeds. One direction per random push.

The measure that failed. C102 and C103 first measured "the same change" with the cosine between embedding change vectors. Checked against my labels, it barely tells "same" from "different" (pitfall 94). The computed halves of those tests are withdrawn; the blind halves stand.

The data

One bend, sized by the edit

C93 followed the push of five edits on three characters along the dose, against random pushes injected at the same place (3,744 trajectories over tokens and taps). At the level of the whole conditioning, every MLP edit turns 45-77 degrees from the smallest to the largest dose, in one direction, almost in a plane, with nearly all the turning at small push length; the random pushes turn 66-88 degrees, less cleanly. None of the four shapes asked (straight, spiral, wave, clip, plus accelerating) fits: "other", one bend, in 9 of 9 edits and 9 of 9 controls.

C100 (60 trajectories, six prompts, doses up to 10) asked whether the shape is the prompt's or the edit's. Rule 1: one bend in 18 of 18 edits and 18 of 18 controls. Rule 2: the total turn of each edit and sign varies by 2-7 degrees over the six prompts, at most 15 in 10 of 10. Median total turn at positive doses: L28 MLP 50.1, L06 MLP 72.6, L14 MLP 80.5, whole layer 6 82.1, the three MLPs together 84.8 degrees. Positive doses from 4 to 10 add nothing new at the whole level; the whole layer 6 leaves the fp16 range at d = 10 for the dwarf (amendment 1).

Past the sign flip the push turns sharply: 22 single-tap clips, all at negative doses. For L06 MLP between -0.8 and -0.9, where its matrices are scaled by 0.2 and 0.1 and the push length jumps tenfold in one step. For the whole layer 6 between -1.5 and -2, which is in part the attention mirror described above. Details in docs/te_shapes2_result.md.

Deeper layers bend less

C101 drew the curve of the MLP and of the attention at every layer, with a random control for the MLP (140 trajectories, gates against C93 at relative error 0). Rule 1: Spearman -0.655 between layer and total turn, permutation p 0.0002. Rule 2: the edit bends less than its control in 24 of 35 layers. Layer 34's control is straight (6 degrees): a push added at the last edited layer reaches the only tap left with no layer in between, so it cannot bend, which is what the controls are for. Attention bends a little less than the MLP (median 60 against 65 degrees). The attention curves past -1 are the algebraic mirror: push length at d = -2 below 1e-5 at every attention layer, and the push at -3 equal to the push at +1. Details in docs/te_shapes_layers_result.md.

Not the massive activations

TEP2 rendered L06 MLP doubled from saved conditionings (the file route of the conditioning-push node) in five versions: the original (C0), the full edit (C1), the edit with the 36 massive entries at the output of layer 6 put back (C2), only the massive change kept (C3), and 36 random entries put back as a control (C4). Per cell, f = DINOv2 distance of X to the original, divided by that of C1.

character seed C2 C3 C4
dwarf 2645751 1.00 0.03 1.00
dwarf 3316624 0.96 0.02 0.97
elf rogue 2645751 0.69 0.05 0.61
elf rogue 3316624 1.41 0.12 0.96
half-orc 2645751 0.98 0.08 0.98
half-orc 3316624 1.00 0.04 1.09

The one cell under 0.80 also drops for the control: it moves whenever anything is restored. On the encoder side the 36 massive entries sit on one token; putting them back keeps about all of the push (cosine 0.97 with the full push). The damage is in the ordinary entries, spread over the tokens. The file route is not bit-identical to the in-graph render (amendment 1, a 5 % tolerance; a ComfyUI update is the likely cause, not verified). Details in docs/te_massive_result.md.

Equal push, unequal pictures

C102 matched four MLP edits (L04, L09, L26, L30) and random pushes at L09 and L26 to the same relative change of the whole conditioning, at two levels anchored on L06 (its push at d = 0.5 and d = 1), on four prompts and three seeds (156 renders). Every target was reached within 1 %. The deep layers needed smaller doses than L06 (L26 about 0.40 and 0.80, L30 about 0.35 and 0.70). Deep moved the picture less than early in 23 of 24 cells.

The question it was built for, whether deep edits change the three seeds in a direction of their own while early edits follow the network, could not be answered: the computed rule came out mixed and the blind one at -0.04, but the deep pictures had barely moved. My notes say so for most deep units: too little change to tell. The random push at L09 changed the seeds as consistently as the L09 edit (blind 0.71 against 0.62). Details in docs/te_depth_control_result.md.

Each perturbation leaves its own change

C103 recalibrated on the picture: every perturbation pushed to a DINOv2 distance of 0.30 on a calibration seed (132 calibration and 96 test renders), with three different random pushes per layer (seeds 9393, 9394, 9395) next to the L09 and L26 edits. The comic page never reached the target at layer 9. R09a was under-matched (0.13). The blind and the computed rules disagreed at both layers.

C104 split the blind question in two, content and style, on the same pictures (55 units):

question layer 9 layer 26
one fixed random push, three seeds, content the same 1.00 (n 5) 0.92 (n 12)
one fixed random push, three seeds, style the same 0.67 (n 6) 0.50 (n 12)
three random pushes, one seed, content the same 0.00 (n 9) 0.25 (n 12)
three random pushes, one seed, style the same 0.56 0.25

The two real edits: content the same across seeds in all their units at both layers. Claude's reading of C103, content from the network and rendering from the perturbation, was not supported at either layer. Details in docs/te_depth_control2_result.md and docs/te_content_style_result.md.

A family resemblance across subjects

C105 took two real edits (L14, L26) and two random pushes (at L09, L26) and calibrated each on eight subjects, so that it moved each picture by a DINOv2 distance of about 0.25 on two calibration seeds (342 calibration renders, 74 test renders at two other seeds). 29 of 32 pairs were reachable; 28 of 29 landed in the matched window (amendment 1). Each blind unit showed four subjects, before and after, with two questions: is the change of content of the same kind in the four pairs, and the change of style?

content within a domain across domains control, different perturbations
real edits 0.38 (n 8) 0.50 (n 6) 0.06 (n 8)
random pushes 0.56 (n 8) 0.58 (n 6) 0.06 (n 8)

Style travels less: real edits 0.19 and 0.25, random pushes 0.44 and 0.25, control 0.00. Of 36 content answers, 3 were "the same", 23 "something similar", 10 "different". My notes name the resemblance: features exaggerated, more flatness, textures picked out, more comics, a sharper division between elements, often with one subject out of the group.

On image-model presets, an earlier test found that a structured preset keeps its direction inside a style domain and loses it across (docs/prereg_domain_specificity.md, 2026-09-25, replication pending). Text-encoder perturbations don't show that boundary. Details in docs/te_domain_transfer_result.md.

Two pairs and an odd one

C106 needed no new renders: 16 trials from C103's text-encoder pictures and 12 from the stage-5 image-model presets of September (seeds 42, 777, 1337, 9999, 4242145; prompts G1-G6), plus 4 repeats. In each trial the seeds were chosen so that grouping by seed was the wrong answer.

exact grouping chance p
all trials 20 of 28 (0.71) 1/15 5.5e-18
text encoder 11 of 16 (0.69) 1/15 3.7e-10
image-model presets 9 of 12 (0.75) 1/15 4.8e-09

Grouped by seed: 0 of 28. Single picture found: 20 of 28 (chance 1/5); pairs correct: 45 of 56. By kind of pair: presets of different families 6 of 9, the same preset at another sign or strength 3 of 3, a text-encoder edit against a random push 2 of 2, two random pushes of the same layer 4 of 7. Exploratory: the failures cluster on random pushes at layer 26 (two trials made only of them, both failed), and every trial containing the L26 edit succeeded. Details in docs/odd_one_out_result.md.

What the embeddings missed

For every C104 unit I had an answer, same or different, and a computed number: the mean cosine between the DINOv2 (or CSD, for style) change vectors of the pictures in it. If the cosine tracked what I see, it would separate the two answers well. It does not: AUC 0.64 for DINOv2 on content, 0.36 for CSD on style, below chance. A cosine between change vectors likely carries a part shared by any change, more realistic, more detailed, which makes different perturbations look alike. This was computed after the rules (pitfall 94). For questions of "the same change", the measure here is the eye.

model:
  checkpoint: krea2_turbo_bf16.safetensors
  weight_dtype: default
  sha256: not recorded — the file is outside the repository

  steps: 9
  cfg: 1.0
  denoise: 1.0
  scheduler: simple
  resolution: 1024x1280
  vae: qwen_image_vae.safetensors
  text_encoder: qwen3vl_4b_bf16.safetensors (CLIPLoader type krea2)

  node: Krea2ConditioningPush (tools/comfyui_krea2_condpush), variant file; conditionings encoded in the ComfyUI venv by the experiment scripts
  version: not recorded — the node is in this repository
  mode: one MLP or attention half of a text-encoder layer, weight x (1 + d); random pushes as per-token random unit directions (seeds 9393, 9394, 9395) x alpha x the per-token norm of the unedited MLP output

  files: [data/te_massive_plan.csv, data/te_depth_control_plan.csv, data/te_depth_control2_plan.csv, data/te_domain_transfer_plan.csv, data/odd_one_out_key.csv]
